_comment: THE ROUTE TABLE THIS APPLICATION SERVES, WRITTEN DOWN SO A MOVE OR A
tools/verify-boot.js assembles the real application and compares what it
actually exposes against this list, in BOTH directions: a route that went
missing fails, and so does one that appeared. The second half is what
makes 'the storefront's routes are not in this process' a build rule
rather than a promise - the day somebody copies a public controller back
across, this check fails before the deployment does.
Every path below is the one it was in the combined repository. The admin
browser modules call them by name and moving a route AND its caller in the
same pass is how a behaviour change gets smuggled into a structural one.
